14581-the-just-and-the-unjust.title: The Just And The Unjust
14581-the-just-and-the-unjust.creator: Vaughan Kester
14581-the-just-and-the-unjust.description: A book by Vaughan Kester. y mornings, with the church bells ringing peacefully beyond the windows of his modest home, and his father in easy undress, just emerged from his weekly bath and pleasantly redolent of strong yellow soap, his feet incased in blue yarn socks--white at toe and heel--and the neckband of his fresh-starched shirt sawing away at the lobes of his freckled ears.

35412-my-unknown-chum-aguecheek.creator: Unknown
35412-my-unknown-chum-aguecheek.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. , in literature, in life and humanity, much that other travellers and other writers and scholars had failed to observe--seeing all with a purity of vision, a clearness of intellect, and recording it with a grace and ease of phrase that suggest that he himself had perhaps been taught by the Angelic Doctor referred to in the closing lines of his last essay.

arxiv-2111-12352.title: The relative index theorem for general first-order elliptic operators
arxiv-2111-12352.creator: Lashi Bandara
arxiv-2111-12352.description: Abstract . The relative index theorem is proved for general first-order elliptic operators that are complete and coercive at infinity over measured manifolds. This extends the original result by Gromov-Lawson for generalised Dirac operators as well as the result of Bär-Ballmann for Dirac-type operators.

arxiv-2112-09764.title: Reflections on the future of machine learning for materials research
arxiv-2112-09764.creator: Naohiro Fujinuma, Brian DeCost, Jason Hattrick-Simpers, Samuel E. Lofland
arxiv-2112-09764.description: Abstract I Abstract Applied machine learning (ML) has rapidly spread throughout the physical sciences; in fact, ML-based data analysis and experimental decision-making has become commonplace. We suggest a shift in the conversation from proving that ML can be used to evaluating how to equitably and effectively implement ML for science.

arxiv-2202-13363.title: Variational Autoencoder with Disentanglement Priors for Low-Resource Task-Specific Natural Language Generation
arxiv-2202-13363.creator: Zhuang Li, Lizhen Qu, Qiongkai Xu, Tongtong Wu, Tianyang Zhan , Gholamreza Haffari, Monash University, Australia, The University of Melbourne, Australia, firstname.lastname@monash.edu, firstname.lastname@unimelb.edu.au, tzha225@student.monash.edu
arxiv-2202-13363.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zhuang Li, Lizhen Qu, Qiongkai Xu, Tongtong Wu, Tianyang Zhan , Gholamreza Haffari, Monash University, Australia, The University of Melbourne, Australia, firstname.lastname@monash.edu, firstname.lastname@unimelb.edu.au, tzha225@student.monash.edu. In this paper, we propose a variational autoencoder with disentanglement priors, VAE-DPrior , for task-specific natural language generation with none or a handful of task-specific labeled examples. In order to tackle compositional generalization across tasks, our model performs disentangled representation learning by introducing a conditional prior for the latent content space and another conditional prior for the latent label space.

arxiv-2206-00972.title: Likelihood criteria for the universe
arxiv-2206-00972.creator: Ezequiel López-Rubio
arxiv-2206-00972.description: Abstract The development of science and technology has progressively demonstrated the ability of humankind to understand and manipulate the physical world, and it has also shown some fundamental limitations to predictability of physical events. This realization has led many thinkers to wonder why the universe has the observed level of regularity.

arxiv-2206-12232.title: A Fundamental Limit of Distributed Hypothesis Testing Under Memoryless Quantization The authors are with École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), 1015 Lausanne, Switzerland. Emails: {yunus.inan, mert.kayaalp, ali.sayed, emre.telatar}@epfl.ch. A short version of this work is presented at IEEE
arxiv-2206-12232.creator: Yunus İnan, , Mert Kayaalp, , Ali H. Sayed, , Emre Telatar
arxiv-2206-12232.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yunus İnan, , Mert Kayaalp, , Ali H. Sayed, , Emre Telatar. We study a distributed hypothesis testing setup where peripheral nodes send quantized data to the fusion center in a memoryless fashion. The expected number of bits sent by each node under the null hypothesis is kept limited. We characterize the optimal decay rate of the mis-detection (type-II error) probability provided that false alarms (type-I error) are rare, and study the tradeoff between the communication rate and maximal type-II error decay rate.

arxiv-2210-08627.title: Long Horizon Planning through Contact using Discrete Search and Continuous Optimization
arxiv-2210-08627.creator: Ramkumar Natarajan, Garrison L.H. Johnston, Nabil Simaan, Maxim Likhachev, Howie Choset
arxiv-2210-08627.description: Abstract Robots often have to perform manipulation tasks in close proximity to people (Fig. 2 ). As such, it is desirable to use a robot arm that has limited joint torques to not injure the nearby person and interacts with the environment to explore new possibilities for completing a task.

arxiv-2305-09568.title: Step-based checkpointing with high-level algorithmic differentiation
arxiv-2305-09568.creator: James R. Maddison
arxiv-2305-09568.description: Abstract Automated code generation allows for a separation between the development of a model, expressed via a domain specific language, and lower level implementation details. Algorithmic differentiation can be applied symbolically at the level of the domain specific language, and the code generator reused to implement code required for an adjoint calculation.

arxiv-2401-04160.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Timmy Ejdetjärn, Oscar Agertz, Göran Östlin, Martin P. Rey, Florent Renaud. arxiv-2405-11816.title: Transfer Learning for CSI-based Positioning with Multi-environment Meta-learning
arxiv-2405-11816.creator: Anastasios Foliadis 1 2 , Mario H. Castañeda Garcia 1 , Richard A. Stirling-Gallacher 1 , Reiner S. Thomä 2
arxiv-2405-11816.description: Abstract Utilizing deep learning (DL) techniques for radio-based positioning of user equipment (UE) through channel state information (CSI) fingerprints has demonstrated significant potential. DL models can extract complex characteristics from the CSI fingerprints of a particular environment and accurately predict the position of a UE.

arxiv-2506-07134.title: Reliable Critics: Monotonic Improvement and Convergence Guarantees for Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2506-07134.creator: Eshwar S. R, Gugan Thoppe, Aditya Gopalan, Gal Dalal
arxiv-2506-07134.description: Abstract Despite decades of research, it remains challenging to correctly use Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms with function approximation. A prime example is policy iteration, whose fundamental guarantee of monotonic improvement collapses even under linear function approximation. To address this issue, we introduce Reliable Policy Iteration (RPI).

arxiv-2506-08320.title: How Good LLM-Generated Password Policies Are? Thanks: *These authors contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2506-08320.creator: Vivek Vaidya*, Aditya Patwardhan*, Ashish Kundu
arxiv-2506-08320.description: Abstract Generative AI technologies, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), are rapidly being adopted across industry, academia, and government sectors, owing to their remarkable capabilities in natural language processing. However, despite their strengths, the inconsistency and unpredictability of LLM outputs present substantial challenges, especially in security-critical domains such as access control.

arxiv-2509-08129.title: torchmil: A PyTorch-based library for deep Multiple Instance Learning
arxiv-2509-08129.creator: Francisco M Castro-Macías fcastro@ugr.es Francisco J Sáez-Maldonado fjaviersaezm@ugr.es Pablo Morales-Álvarez pablomorales@ugr.es Rafael Molina rms@decsai.ugr.es * Corresponding author Department of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, University of Granada, Spain Research Centre for Inform
arxiv-2509-08129.description: Abstract Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) is a powerful framework for weakly supervised learning, particularly useful when fine-grained annotations are unavailable. Despite growing interest in deep MIL methods, the field lacks standardized tools for model development, evaluation, and comparison, which hinders reproducibility and accessibility. To address this, we present torchmil , an open-source Python library built on PyTorch.

arxiv-2601-17243.title: Estimation of temperature and precipitation uncertainties using quantile neural networks
arxiv-2601-17243.description: Abstract Extreme events pose significant risks and are challenging to predict. Assessing climate hazards requires placing quantitative constraints on geophysical fields under observable but fluctuating conditions. We propose a framework for estimating uncertainties—a ReLU-bias loss quantile neural network (RBLQNN)—with two novel modifications to the loss function to enforce uniform quantile accuracy and reduce degenerate predicted probability distributions.

arxiv-2602-18528.title: Audio-Visual Continual Test-Time Adaptation without Forgetting
arxiv-2602-18528.creator: Sarthak Kumar Maharana, Akshay Mehra, Bhavya Ramakrishna, Yunhui Guo, Guan-Ming Su
arxiv-2602-18528.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Sarthak Kumar Maharana, Akshay Mehra, Bhavya Ramakrishna, Yunhui Guo, Guan-Ming Su. Audio-visual continual test-time adaptation involves continually adapting a source audio-visual model at test-time, to unlabeled non-stationary domains, where either or both modalities can be distributionally shifted, which hampers online cross-modal learning and eventually leads to poor accuracy. While previous works have tackled this problem, we find that SOTA methods suffer from catastrophic forgetting where the model’s performance drops well below the source model due to continual parameter updates at test-time.

pmc-10630429.creator: Duncan D Smith, Mark A Adams, Amanda M Salvi, Christopher P Krieg, Cécile Ané, Katherine A McCulloh, Thomas J Givnish
pmc-10630429.description: Tradeoffs between the energetic benefits and costs of traits can shape species and trait distributions along environmental gradients. Here we test predictions based on such tradeoffs using survival, growth, and 50 photosynthetic, hydraulic, and allocational traits of ten Eucalyptus species grown in four common gardens along an 8-fold gradient in precipitation/pan evaporation (P/Ep) in Victoria, Australia.

pmc-10707789.title: Ursolic Acid’s Alluring Journey: One Triterpenoid vs. Cancer Hallmarks
pmc-10707789.creator: Youness Limami, Aline Pinon, Hicham Wahnou, Mounia Oudghiri, Bertrand Liagre, Alain Simon, Raphaël Emmanuel Duval, Akihito Yokosuka
pmc-10707789.description: Cancer is a multifactorial disease characterized by various hallmarks, including uncontrolled cell growth, evasion of apoptosis, sustained angiogenesis, tissue invasion, and metastasis, among others. Traditional cancer therapies often target specific hallmarks, leading to limited efficacy and the development of resistance. Thus, there is a growing need for alternative strategies that can address multiple hallmarks concomitantly.

pmc-11383490.title: A rare presentation of hematosalpinx with torsion in a thirteen year-old virgin: a case report
pmc-11383490.creator: Shivani Raju, Shravya Kashyap, Afnan W M Jobran, Shrivarshini K, Shravya N
pmc-11383490.description: A medical condition called hematosalpinx causes an accumulation of blood within the fallopian tube. It is usually seen in patients with ectopic pregnancy. Inflammatory disease of the pelvis, tubal cancer, pelvic trauma, and endometriosis are further causes. Here, we report a unique case of hematosalpinx with associated tubal torsion in a 13-year-old female lacking any previously reported contributing causes.

pmc-11601903.creator: Yogita Sharma, Robin Lo, Viktor N. Tomilin, Kotdaji Ha, Holly Deremo, Aishwarya V. Pareek, Wuxing Dong, Xiaohui Liao, Svetlana Lebedeva, Vivek Charu, Neeraja Kambham, Kerim Mutig, Oleh Pochynyuk, Vivek Bhalla
pmc-11601903.description: Mutations in the CLCNKB gene (1p36), encoding the basolateral chloride channel ClC-Kb, cause type 3 Bartter syndrome. We identified a family with a mixed Bartter/Gitelman phenotype and early-onset kidney failure and by employing a candidate gene approach, identified what we believe is a novel homozygous mutation (CLCNKB c.499G>T [p.Gly167Cys]) in exon 6 of CLCNKB in the index patient.

It is characterized by the presence of anti-ribonucleoprotein (anti-U1RNP) antibodies.

pmc-13249912.title: Excluded-stomach Perforation after Roux-en-Y and One-anastomosis Gastric Bypass: A Systematic Review with Video-illustrated Case Report
pmc-13249912.creator: Mohamed Hany, Ala Wafa, Mona S. Youssef, Mohamed H. Zidan, Hashem Altabbaa, Hazem Al-Momani, Dina M. Hafez, Walid El Ansari, Mohamed Samir
pmc-13249912.description: Gastric remnant or duodenal perforation after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) or one-anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) is rare and may be missed radiologically. We systematically reviewed PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science and included 26 reports (34 patients), alongside a video-illustrated late OAGB case. Mean age was 49 years, 73.5% were female, and BMI at presentation was 33.
